name: tradebee
description: v26.6.26 A unified Tradebee Website Builder Open API skill for mapping an explicit Tradebee platform data-operation request to the correct Tradebee action. Use it only when the user clearly wants to operate on Tradebee blogs, blog groups, FAQs, FAQ groups, custom pages, products, product groups, inquiries, recent visitors, keyword rankings, or tenant HTML rule retrieval, and the target object type matches this skill. Do not use it for generic 'find', 'show', 'check', 'update', or 'delete' requests outside Tradebee platform data context. For all `*_update` actions, the skill also automatically reads the current record and writes a local JSON backup file before sending the update request.

action.description: Required. Selects which Tradebee OpenAPI capability to execute. Route only after the Tradebee data domain and object type are explicit. Use `*-read` for Tradebee requests to read/list/find/check/query/analyze existing Tradebee data; use `*-create` for Tradebee requests to create/add/publish new Tradebee content; use `*-update` for Tradebee requests to modify one explicit existing Tradebee record; use `*-delete` for Tradebee requests to delete one explicit existing Tradebee record or one explicitly confirmed Tradebee ID list. Do not infer destructive actions from vague requests. For every `*-update` action, execution also includes an automatic pre-update read of the current record and a local JSON backup file write before the Tradebee update request is sent. Route by object type: HTML rule retrieval -> `rule-get`, blog/article -> `blog-*`, blog group/category -> `bloggroup-*`, FAQ article -> `faq-*`, FAQ group/category -> `faqgroup-*`, custom page -> `custompage-*`, product -> `products-*`, product group/category -> `productsgroup-*`, inquiries/leads -> `inquiry-read`, visitors/IP activity -> `visitor-recent`, keyword performance/top N rankings -> `keywords-rank`.

blog.description: Required by `blog-create` and `blog-update`. This object contains the blog fields to create or update. For `blog-create`, send a complete new blog payload. For `blog-update`, `blog_id` is required and every other field is optional: omit any field you do not want to change.

bloggroup_id.description: Blog group ID. For `blog-create`, this field is required. For `blog-update`, omit it if the blog should stay in its current group. Only send it when the user explicitly wants to move the blog to another group.

publisher.description: Publisher name, up to 100 characters. Omit it in `blog-update` if the publisher should stay unchanged.

publication_date.description: Display publication date in `yyyy/M/d` format, for example `2026/4/24`. For `blog-create`, if omitted, the server uses the current date. For `blog-update`, omit it if the publication date should stay unchanged.

title.description: Blog title shown to users, up to 500 characters. For `blog-create`, this is required. For `blog-update`, omit it if the title should stay unchanged.

cover_image.description: Cover image payload, up to 500 kB. For `blog-create`, this field is required. For `blog-update`, omit it if the cover image should stay unchanged.

name.description: Image file label used only to identify this image inside the payload.

base64.description: Base64 image data with MIME prefix, for example `image/jpeg;base64,...`.

tags.description: Keyword tags. For `blog-create`, provide 1 to 6 keyword tags. Each tag must contain 3 to 50 characters. For `blog-update`, omit this field if tags should stay unchanged.

summary.description: Blog summary as plain text, up to 500 characters. For `blog-create`, this is required. For `blog-update`, omit it if the summary should stay unchanged.

confirmation.description: Required by `blog-create`, `blog-update`, `blog-delete`, `bloggroup-create`, `bloggroup-update`, `bloggroup-delete`, `custompage-create`, `custompage-update`, `custompage-delete`, `faq-create`, `faq-update`, `faq-delete`, `faqgroup-create`, `faqgroup-update`, `faqgroup-delete`, `productsgroup-create`, `productsgroup-update`, `productsgroup-delete`, `products-create`, `products-update`, and `products-delete`. This object proves the user explicitly approved the exact destructive or high-impact change after seeing the real payload or ID list. For all `*-update` actions, that approval must also cover the automatic local backup file write of the current record and requested update payload before execution. Never set it automatically before showing the user the final action details.

approved.description: Must be `true` only after the user explicitly confirms the action. If the user has not clearly approved the exact payload or ID list, do not send this action.

summary.description: Required human-readable confirmation note that restates the action, language, and the exact payload or product IDs shown to the user before execution. This must match what the user approved.

For `faqgroup-delete`, these are FAQ group IDs. For `productsgroup-delete`, these are product group IDs. For `products-delete`, these are product IDs.

language.description: Required for most content operations and for `rule-get`. This is the exact site language code to operate on, such as `en` or `fr`. Do not guess, translate, or invent this value. First call `languages-get`, show the returned language list to the user, and copy one exact `language` value from that list after the user confirms it. When generating any HTML fragment such as `blog.description`, `faq.answer`, `products.description`, `productsgroup.section.top`, `productsgroup.section.bottom`, or `custompage.content`, call `rule-get` first with the exact same selected `language` and the exact matching `scene` value. backup.description: Returned by `blog-update`, `bloggroup-update`, `custompage-update`, `productsgroup-update`, and `products-update` when the automatic pre-update backup succeeds. It includes backup file storage metadata, the raw read API response, the extracted pre-change snapshot, and a best-effort `restore_payload` that can be passed back into the same `*-update` action to revert the change. The local backup JSON file also persists `confirmation_summary`, `requested_update_payload`, and `restore_limitations` alongside those returned structures, and may therefore contain sensitive business or personal data from the record being changed. If the backup snapshot cannot be captured or the backup file cannot be written, the update action must fail instead of modifying data.
